newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-POLITICS OVERSHADOW CHAMPIONS' CUP CLASH IN SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-POLITICS OVERSHADOW CHAMPIONS' CUP CLASH IN SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: South Africa's Orlando Pirates continue their defence of the African Champions' Cup on Sunday with a controversial clash against Nigeria's Shooting Stars.
The quarter-final first leg in Bloemfontein is clouded with political overtones following Nigeria's refusal to play in South Africa in January's African Nations' Cup finals.

The decision, which led to a four-year ban on the national team by the Confederation of African Football, followed South Africa's condemnation of the execution of Nigerian writer Ken Saro-Wiwa and nine others last year.

South Africa withdrew an invitation to Nigeria to play in a four-national international tournament in November. Nigerian leader Sani Abacha responded by stopping the Super Eagles from defending their Nations' Cup title in South Africa.
The feud took a further turn last week when the South African High Commission in Lagos initially refused to issue visas for Stars' visit but later relented after instructions from Pretoria.

Nigeria also rejected an invitation from South Africa to play in this year's Four Nations Cup, along with Australia, Ghana and the home team. They have been replaced by Kenya in the tournament, which starts on September 14.
Away from politics, out-of-form Pirates face a tough test because the Ibadan side romped through the opening two rounds.
Pirates have key defender Gavin Lane back after injury in time to deal with the attacking capabilities of Sam Pam and Patrick Mancha, both occasional Nigerian internationals.
Zamalek of Egypt host Morocco's COD Meknes in Cairo and surprise side Diaraf Dakar visit CS Sfaxien of Tunisia in other Champions' Cup games.
Diaraf caused a major upset in the second round by eliminating ASEC Abidjan of the Ivory Coast.
Angola's Petro Atletico face JS Kabylie of Algeria in Luanda on Sunday in the other quarter-final.
